system.name: DARTH-PUM
system.one_liner: a general-purpose hybrid processing-using-memory architecture that integrates analog and digital PUM to execute full kernels in memory

content.subject: how an analog PUM crossbar performs a 2x2 matrix by 2x1 vector multiply via conductances, row voltages, and column currents

relations.what: the same matrix values are programmed as conductances G=1/R
each row's input value multiplies that column's programmed conductance (Ohm's law)
the resulting currents on each column are summed
the accumulated column currents equal the matrix-vector product entries, matching the arithmetic result

panels.label: (a) Matrix-vector multiply
panels.differs: the reference computation done as plain arithmetic on coloured number boxes, with no circuit

panels.label: (b) Analog matrix-vector multiply
panels.differs: the same computation realized physically as a crossbar: conductances encode the matrix, row voltages encode the vector, and Ohm's/Kirchhoff's laws perform the multiply-accumulate

steps.what: matrix values (5,9,8,7) are programmed into the crossbar as resistances/conductances G=1/R
input vector values (2, 7) are applied as voltages along the rows and multiplied by each cell's conductance
the per-cell products (currents) are accumulated down each column
each column's accumulated current equals one output entry, matching the reference arithmetic result (66, 67)

values.what: the worked 2x2-by-2x1 example itself: inputs 2 and 7, matrix entries 5, 9, 8, 7, conductances 1/5, 1/9, 1/8, 1/7, and results 66 and 67
values.linked_by: colour, carried consistently from the crossbar labels into the verification equations at the bottom
values.result_cells: the two black result boxes (66, 67) in panel (a) and the two summed equations below panel (b)

content.key_idea: An analog crossbar reproduces a matrix-vector multiply physically: matrix values become programmed conductances, input-vector values become row voltages, Ohm's law multiplies them at each junction, and Kirchhoff's current law accumulates the products down each column into the result.
content.reading_order: panel (a) first, reading the plain arithmetic left to right; then panel (b), following circled steps 1 (programming) then 2a (multiply along rows) then 2b (accumulate down columns) to 3 (result checked against panel (a))

summary: This figure walks through how an analog processing-using-memory crossbar physically performs a matrix-vector multiply, alongside a plain-arithmetic reference. Panel (a) shows the reference: a 2x1 vector [2,7] times a 2x2 matrix [[5,9],[8,7]] equals [66,67], computed as ordinary arithmetic in coloured boxes. Panel (b) shows the same computation realized in a crossbar, narrated by four circled steps: (1) the matrix values are programmed into the crossbar as conductances 1/5, 1/9, 1/8, 1/7; (2a) the input vector's values are applied as row voltages and multiplied by each conductance (Ohm's law); (2b) the resulting currents are accumulated down each column (Kirchhoff's current law); and (3) each column's total current equals one output entry, verified against panel (a) by two colour-coded equations. The figure demonstrates that electrical multiply-accumulate reproduces exact matrix-vector arithmetic.
